text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx error rate observed for service 'text-gen' behind ELB app/text-gen-prod in eu-west-2. 5m error rate = 18% (baseline <0.5%). Link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/alerts/5178901234 :rotating_light:

sven: I'm on it. paging @cassie (sre) and @ryan (network). Is this regional or global?

cassie: seeing it across two AZs in eu-west-2, but az-a has much higher 502/504s. ELB target health shows many targets draining/0/5 failed checks.

maya: getting customer reports (SLA pings). lia, can you surface any high-impact customers?

lia (cust-succ): a couple of enterprise customers reported 502s from EU users. No official escalations yet but support tickets coming in.

ryan: checking VPC flow logs and our edge proxies — not seeing packet drops, looks like upstream instances are returning errors. Could be EBS or instance-level saturation.

cassie: full snapshot of server metrics:
```
ELB 5xx: 18%
Instance CPU avg (az-a): 72%
Instance CPU avg (az-b): 45%
Disk iops (az-a): 98th pct spike
Kernel dmesg: occasional block commit timeouts
ELB target health: 12/30 healthy in az-a, 28/30 healthy in az-b
```

sven: sounds like az-a degradation. Runbook suggests shifting Route53 weights away from eu-west-2 to eu-west-1 for customer-facing endpoints. We need to avoid mass DNS TTL churn though.

ops-bot: runbook-step: route53-weight-shift started by sven at 5178901301.

cassie: before we shift DNS, quick mitigation: put ELB in az-a into failover/force-drain to stop routing traffic there, then spin up additional targets in az-b or another region.

maya: I can trigger ASG scale-up in eu-west-2 az-b and eu-west-1. Command I'm about to run:
```
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name text-gen-prod-asg --desired-capacity 60 --region eu-west-2
```

sven: do it. Also change ELB connection draining timeout lower so unhealthy targets stop faster (60s).

cassie: initiating graceful drain on elb-target-group arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/text-gen-tg/abc123 (az-a)

ryan: investigating EBS metrics for az-a instances: elevated queue length, increased latency on a few volumes. Might be transient EBS degradation in that AZ. Opening AWS support case now. Case#: 1234567890.

lia (cust-succ): noted — informing affected customers we are routing around EU-AZ issues and expect recovery in ~15-30m.

sven: timeline: 00:00 root detection; +6m scale-up and drain; +12m start DNS weight shift if ELB health not recovering. Keep updates concise.

cassie: quick check of app logs shows a spike in disk write errors from background flush job around the same time. Example log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:31:12Z ERROR storage.FlushJob failed to flush: write I/O timeout
2026-03-15T02:31:13Z WARN disk_io: retrying
```

maya: scaling done in az-b and eu-west-1, new instances healthy in az-b. ELB still sending ~30% traffic to az-a until connections drain.

sven: starting Route53 weighted shift (20% -> 0% to eu-west-2; distribute to eu-west-1 & eu-west-3). TTL on record 60s. ops-bot log?

ops-bot: route53-change submitted: https://console.aws.amazon.com/route53/changes/CA1234567890 

cassie: ELB target health in az-a still shows flapping; some instances recover then fail healthchecks. This aligns with EBS noisy neighbor/IOPS issues.

ryan: AWS support replies: "We are investigating increased EBS backend tail latency in eu-west-2 for a subset of volumes. Recomended to move critical workloads to another AZ or region."

sven: decision: keep weight shift in progress. Do not perform full region failover yet (need to monitor error rate). Start incident bridge for handoff to night SRE. Bridge: https://zoom.redwood/incident/5178901234

cassie: summary for bridge and handoff: cause - elevated EBS tail latency in eu-west-2 AZ-a causing backend write errors -> app 502s; impact - customer-facing 502s for EU users, partial region; mitigations - drain az-a targets, ASG scale-up, Route53 weighted shift, AWS case opened; next actions - if error rate >5% after 20m, start regional failover plan.

sven: I'm handing off to night oncall @cassie. I'll remain on-call for major escalations. Please post short updates every 10m in this thread.

cassie: acknowledged. joining bridge.

lia (cust-succ): emailed affected customers with status and next update ETA 30m.

maya: note: we saw a small increase in latency for embeddings calls but most impact on text-gen where writes to local cache happen. Could be mitigated by toggling cache write-behavior. I'll open a deploy to disable cache-backfill on new instances as a low-risk mitigation:
```
./deploy-tool promote --service text-gen --env prod --change "disable-cache-backfill"
```

ops-bot: change request created CR-9876, deploy queued. Estimated 5m to ramp.

cassie: after the weight shift error rate dropped to 6% from 18% (metric link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/graph/517890). Still above target. Continue ramping traffic away and monitor logs.

sven: good. if AWS indicates widespread AZ degradation for >1h, we'll open a P1 with execs and initiate broader region failover. For now keep containment.

ryan: note to docs - create a post-incident task to add EBS-tail-latency playbook and add automated target draining when AWS EBS issues detected.

cassie: 10m update: error rate 4.2% after finishing weight shift and deploy. ASG new instances healthy. AWS still acknowledges issue but volume of affected EBS decreased.

lia (cust-succ): sending customers update: service partially restored; still monitoring; expected full restoration next update in 30m.

sven: thanks all. leaving the thread for now, on-call rotation notes attached to incident ticket. If anything spikes >10% reopen urgent channel. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (status: mitigated) at 5178901367. Postmortem required: link https://incidents.redwood/5178901234/postmortem

cassie: creating initial timeline and recording playbook gaps.

maya: will follow up on cache-backfill change impact.

ryan: will file AWS retro and follow-up with support case closure.

lia (cust-succ): will compile customer impact list for postmortem.

--- end of thread ---
